newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/3Com call buyers seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/3Com call buyers seen.

text.p: Options on 3Com Corp were busy as the stock extended its recent decline after a couple of brokerage firms lowered their investment ratings.
At about 1400 CST/2000 GMT, the stock was down 2-7/8 points at 49-3/8 on more than 23.5 million shares. The stock reached a session low of 47-1/4.
Traders said options investors were largely buying calls in the face of the stock's decline.
The 3Com February 50 call traded about 7,850 contracts. The option was down 1-1/2 at 2-3/8 and had open interest of 339 contracts through Thursday.
3Com shares have dropped sharply every day this week. They ended last week at about 67.
On Friday, Cowen & Co lowered its rating on the network systems company to buy from strong buy and Oppenheimer & Co cut its rating to market perform from buy.
Other busy 3Com calls included the February 55, with volume of about 4,375 contracts, the February 60 with volume of nearly 1,000 and the March 55 call with volume of roughly 1,100 contracts.
But nearly every call in the entire series traded.
The heaviest put action was in the February 50, where more than 3,550 contracts changed hands.
Traders said volatilities on the 3Com options continued to rise as the stock extended its decline.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer, said volatility Friday was around 56, compared to a six-month average of about 49.
In other trading, a spread in a couple of Staples Inc calls crossed on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange.
The Staples February 17-1/2 call traded 2,200 contracts and the March 17-1/2 traded about 2,300.
The February 17-1/2 traded at 2-1/2 and the March 17-1/2 at 2-5/8.
"It looks like it could be a rollover February to March for 1/8 of a point," Schwartz said.
Elsewhere, Intel Corp options on the American Stock Exchange were active again as the shares staged a recovery from recent losses.

The chip maker's stock was up 2-1/2 at 155-5/8 on volume of more than 13 million shares in afternoon trading. The stock reached almost 165 on Tuesday before beginning a slide that ended at 150-3/4 Thursday afternoon.
Outside of the regular Intel options, several Intel LEAPS (long term equity anticipation securities) were busy, led by the January 1998 130 put, which traded about 4,275 contracts.
The January 1998 140 put traded 2,510.
On the call side, the January 1998 205 call traded a little more than 1,900 contracts. The option, which had open interest of 6,027 contracts, traded at 8-1/4.
